title: Fresh reports, head to head: the product against a frontier LLM on threat reports neither has seen
request: the product owner asked for a bigger test set, built head to head against a frontier model (2026-10-28), because a zero-shot frontier LLM may make the approach pointless: the product matches ChatGPT-4 on CTI-TAA but trails GPT-5 on AthenaBench (docs 21.3.26), and public benchmark reports may be remembered by the models
question: On threat reports published after the frontier model's training cutoff and not cited by ATT&CK, how often does each of (a) the product, (b) a current frontier LLM zero-shot, (c) their registered combination put the right ATT&CK group first, and how many names does each give, right and wrong?
role: test set: evaluation only, never tuned on, never a training or calibration set; local only (the text belongs to each vendor; CISA advisories are US government works); not redistributed

set.sources: 15 research blogs and CISA advisories, listed by sitemap or feed (SOURCES in the builder): Unit 42, Microsoft Security blog, ESET WeLiveSecurity, Securelist, Check Point Research, SentinelLabs, Cisco Talos, Zscaler ThreatLabz, Proofpoint threat insight, Google Threat Intelligence, Trend Micro research, Symantec (security.com threat intelligence), Recorded Future research, Volexity, CISA cybersecurity advisories
set.candidates: data/benchmarks/fresh/candidates.json, listed 2026-10-28T14:20Z, 746 URLs (sha256 89bc60829df1269581d5ec5d28967abc490160a0604c0881b79fcf95f717a794); URLs MITRE ATT&CK 20.0 cites anywhere and URLs of the CTI-HAL, Elastic, vendor, advisory, campaign, CTI-TAA and AthenaBench sets are left out
set.window: published 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-27 by the date the page states (else the URL's or the listing's date); Claude Opus 5.5's training cutoff is June 2026
set.actor_names: ATT&CK 20.0 group names and aliases (and the short form of a '... Group' name) plus the MISP galaxy threat-actor list (data/benchmarks/fresh/misp_threat_actor.json, sha256 4db1bf035a6ce5b3859c8da8047b933291ab4992cce6d9e1810eef8e572a93e6, CC0/BSD-2), mapped to ATT&CK groups as in actor_dictionary; names that are also ATT&CK software names never count; vendor cluster codes (UNC1234, Storm-1234, TA123, CL-STA-1234, Earth/Water/Void names, ...) that are no ATT&CK alias are actors ATT&CK does not document
set.label_rule: label_report on the post as reported, before masking: known = the leading ATT&CK group has >= 3 mentions, >= 2x the next ATT&CK group, more than any other actor, and is named in the title or the first 10 statements; open set = an actor ATT&CK does not document leads the same way and no ATT&CK group is named more than once (a MISP actor linked to an ATT&CK group is left out); at least 15 statements; everything else is left out
set.masking: every actor name the rule knows and every vendor cluster code becomes 'the adversary' in the statements and the title (ATT&CK software names are kept); the benchmark's own anonymiser runs on top
set.caps: at most 8 known reports per group, newest first; a report sharing >= half its statements with an earlier kept report is a duplicate
set.label_review: before any system runs on the set, the open-set reports and the known reports labelled only through MISP names are read against the post's own attribution; a report whose label disagrees with the vendor's stated attribution is excluded (never relabelled) in a logged amendment (data/benchmarks/fresh/amendments.json, committed before the runs)

arms.product: the current defaults at the commit that registers the amendments, local pipeline (no API key, local LLM off, technique head service on): scripts/attribution_benchmark.py --report-set fresh --cti-hal data/benchmarks/fresh/reports.jsonl --open-set data/benchmarks/fresh/open_set.jsonl --anonymize strict --report-observations 0 (headline), and the names and tradecraft readings
arms.llm: anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 via OpenRouter (first on OpenRouter's general benchmark board, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 58.4 on 2026-10-28; the product owner asked for the best model per OpenRouter's benchmarks), reasoning effort medium, structured output, one call per report, default sampling: scripts/fresh_llm_attribution.py (sha256 dafc26d24139fc8eef2d0959faee40f87b830a3eb4533a534afc8e3bc3684608) at the strict reading, the same statements the product reads; the tradecraft reading is secondary and runs only if the credit allows
arms.combination: scripts/fresh_h2h_score.py (sha256 f4b4218f266b1ec8c1f47e798dfa05dd22874d8ac9cbe7c5a184bf5d5465a351), no fitting: first choice = the LLM's first candidate when the product ranks it in its top five, else the product's leader; a name only when the product's leader and the LLM's first candidate agree and the LLM decides to name

metrics: known reports: first choice right, top three right, per-group macro first choice; names given, right and wrong; open set: every name is wrong. Paired bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 report resamples, seed 7) and exact McNemar for each pair of first-choice rates

reading_guide.first_choice: 'clearly ahead' = at least 0.10 higher with the bootstrap interval of the difference above 0; otherwise 'comparable'
reading_guide.names: wrong names are read with the number of names given: an arm that names less is not safer by that alone; the safer arm has fewer wrong names in total and per name given
reading_guide.consequence: LLM clearly ahead and not less safe -> recommend rebuilding attribution around the LLM, the product's evidence and naming gate as the explanation and safety layer; LLM clearly ahead but less safe -> recommend the combination if it keeps the product's wrong-name level; comparable or product ahead -> the approach stands, the LLM optional

caveats: labels are the vendors' own attribution (vendors can be wrong or disagree); a post in the window may retell research from before the cutoff; the cutoff is the model maker's stated one; one sample per report; the product's ATT&CK 20.0 knowledge legitimately includes earlier reports on the same actors (so does the model's training)
cost: downloads free (about 750 pages at one request per second, approved 2026-10-28); product runs about 2-4 hours on the laptop; the LLM arm needs an OpenRouter top-up (1.20 USD left on 2026-10-28) and is priced by --dry-run on the built set before any spend

amendments.made_before: any system (product or LLM) ran on any report of the set; only label counts of a preliminary build were seen
amendments.reason: the July-October window gave about 20 known-group reports and 30 open-set reports from the 15 sources (fresh reporting mostly names new clusters), too few to show a 0.10 first-choice difference (about 120 needed); the product owner chose a longer window with an earlier-cutoff model plus more sources
amendments.llm: main arm: openai/gpt-5.6-sol (OpenRouter's stated knowledge cutoff 2026-02-16), reasoning effort medium, the same prompt and schema, on every report; secondary arm: anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 on the reports published from 2026-07-01 (fresh_llm_attribution.py --since 2026-07-01). The reading guide applies to the main arm; the combination is scored with each model on its reports
amendments.sources_added: approved by the product owner on 2026-10-29 and listable with dates: Seqrite, Bitdefender Labs, Silent Push, Fortinet threat research, Arctic Wolf, Rapid7, Hunt.io; Google is also listed from its blog sitemap and Recorded Future from its sitemap (their feeds reach back only to June/July). Approved but not used: AhnLab ASEC (serves a browser check), Sophos (timeouts), Huntress and HarfangLab (403), Positive Technologies (certificate error), Genians (Korean only), Kroll and Intezer (no threat-research listing)
amendments.bug_fix: the vendor cluster-code pattern missed five-digit codes (UAT-11587, Storm-10001, UAC-10001, TAG-10001); fixed before the build
amendments.downloads: a rate limit, a server error or a '202 Accepted' holding page is retried once at one request per 5 s; Check Point answered 24 pages with '202 Accepted' again (bot protection, not bypassed): left out
